files_read: directory listing (the two scripts and three TSVs are named in the README as its raw inputs and were not read)
symptom: A detector was evaluated over an entire corpus under a newly wired input source, and it never fired once. The run completed, produced a status for every item, and the statuses were legal values — abstain and no-finding — so the output had the shape of a measurement whose answer happened to be negative. Nothing in it distinguished a detector that looked and found nothing from a detector that could not look at all, which is what it was: the query underneath matched zero of the things it was supposed to match, for every item, unconditionally.
mechanism_as_described: The clause that fetched the per-position typing called a predicate with the position argument left unbound, in a slot the predicate requires to be bound on entry. The call therefore matched nothing rather than erroring. Downstream of it sat a threshold requiring at least two typeable positions before the detector will return a determinate verdict, so zero matches meant the threshold could never be cleared, which meant the status was abstain everywhere, which meant no firing anywhere. Each stage behaved correctly given its input; the failure was that the first stage's empty result is also a legitimate state, and every stage after it treats emptiness as information rather than as absence of information.
detection_path: The document records the detection as an inference from the shape of the result rather than from any error: a detector that reads abstain or no-finding everywhere cannot produce a perfect diagonal against an independent quantity, so the uniformity of the first run's output is itself the evidence that it was measuring nothing, and the later numbers could only have come from a run after the fix. The prose does not say what first prompted the check. Once re-sourced, the probe was separately validated before being trusted on data where the comparison quantity does not exist: the same quantity was recomputed independently and matched the pipeline's own value on 119 of 119 items with zero mismatches, and only then applied to the two corpora where no pipeline value was available to check against.
consequence: The run's output was an input to a pending decision about whether one of two candidate wirings is a redundant recomputation of a quantity the system already reports. An all-abstain column would have entered that decision as a measurement. The document does not state which way the buggy numbers would have pushed the decision; it states only that they could not have produced the observed result, and it keeps the buggy run's output as the witness that the defect existed and that the fix changed something. The corrected run answers the redundancy question cleanly — one wiring is exactly coextensive with the existing quantity across 1,197 eligible items with zero off-diagonal, the other diverges on 36 — and the document is careful to bound what that licenses: the coextension is definitional rather than independent confirmation, and non-redundancy is not reliability.

extraction_notes.boundary_rule_applied: UNIT — prose REPORTS an instance. A provenance section states that the first run of this analysis used a defective clause, names the defect (an unbound argument in a mode-restricted position), states its effect (zero matches for every item, hence abstain everywhere, hence no firing), and reasons about what its output could and could not have produced. Specific occurrence, not a discussion of the concept.
extraction_notes.selection_rule_applied: One incident per directory, fullest DESCRIBED mechanism. NOT extracted: (a) a correction of an earlier overclaim in the same document — two of the three corpora used for replication are twins, the same seed material through different backends, so they are correlated draws rather than independent ones, and the earlier reading of the result as triple replication is withdrawn and restated as one independent corpus plus one correlated pair. This is a genuine second instance, of a claim that read as stronger evidence than it was, and it is self-corrected in place; it loses on the selection rule because its mechanism is one paragraph where the extracted incident's is a stated causal chain. (b) The document's several scope caveats — definitional coextension is not confirmation, non-redundancy is not reliability, the determinacy restriction drops about half of each twin — are guards against misreading rather than reported occurrences.
extraction_notes.redaction_note: Predicate names, argument-mode notation, module and file names, the tracker identifiers, the ruling labels, and all item identifiers are stripped from the coder-facing fields. Counts and the zero-off-diagonal result are retained; the impossibility argument that constitutes the detection path depends on them.

metadata.incident_location_note: The directory's subject is a cross-tabulation feeding a pending ruling. The incident appears in a provenance section auditing this analysis's own earlier run. Reading it as 'incidental' would also be defensible — it is a defect tripped over en route to the real subject — but the section is explicitly a self-audit of the numbers being reported, so I applied the more specific label.
